Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData builds a CSV string with a header row that has extra trailing commas (A,B,C,,) and a data row with five values (a,b,c,d,e).
  - It parses using CSVFormat.EXCEL.withHeader(), which tells the parser to read the first record as the header.

- How parsing proceeds:
  - CSVParser.parse(String, CSVFormat) constructs a CSVParser with the given format.
  - CSVParser’s constructor calls initializeHeader().
  - initializeHeader() checks the format’s header configuration:
    - withHeader() with no arguments sets an empty header array, which signals initializeHeader() to read the first record from the input as the header.
    - The headerRecord thus becomes ["A", "B", "C", "", ""] from the first line A,B,C,,.
  - It then builds a header name-to-index map by iterating the headerRecord:
    - For each header cell, it checks:
      - containsHeader: whether the map already has this header name.
      - emptyHeader: whether the header is null or blank.
    - If a header name is a duplicate and either it is not empty OR it is empty and allowMissingColumnNames is false, it throws:
      - throw new IllegalArgumentException("The header contains a duplicate name: \"" + header + "\" in " + Arrays.toString(headerRecord));
    - Because there are two empty header names ("" twice), the second "" is seen as a duplicate.
    - CSVFormat.EXCEL, as currently defined, does not enable allowMissingColumnNames (it is inherited from DEFAULT as false).
    - Therefore, encountering the second empty header triggers the IllegalArgumentException with message The header contains a duplicate name: "" in [A, B, C, , ].

- Why this fails for EXCEL:
  - Real-world Excel exports commonly include unlabeled trailing columns, producing empty header names when using the first row as the header.
  - The bug report states that CSVFormat.EXCEL should ignore empty header names. In code, that corresponds to allowing missing column names so they do not trigger the duplicate-name exception.
  - Currently, EXCEL is defined as DEFAULT.withIgnoreEmptyLines(false), which keeps allowMissingColumnNames = false.
  - This mismatch causes initializeHeader() to reject duplicate empty header names for EXCEL and throw, making the test fail.

- Fault localization:
  - CSVParser.initializeHeader(): the duplicate-empty-header check throws unless allowMissingColumnNames is true.
  - CSVFormat.EXCEL definition: does not set allowMissingColumnNames to true, so parsing headers with multiple empty names fails for EXCEL.
  - Secondary: CSVFormat.withHeader(String...) enforces duplicate checks only for explicitly supplied headers; here the header is read from the file, so the throwing path is exclusively in initializeHeader().

- Root cause:
  - The EXCEL format does not enable allowMissingColumnNames, but it should for compatibility with Excel’s empty unlabeled columns. This causes initializeHeader() to treat repeated empty header names as invalid duplicates and throw an IllegalArgumentException during parser construction.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
